subject: Oasis Restaurant Extended Hours Public Hearing
overview: The Council held a lengthy public hearing regarding a special permit for extended hours at Oasis Restaurant and continued discussions on targeted charter amendments. Members also heard testimony from city clerical and DPW workers regarding stalled contract negotiations and passed a resolution supporting secure firearm storage.

items.title: Announcements and Accolades
items.summary: The Council recognized Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month and Jewish American Heritage Month.

items.title: Reports of Committees: Ordinances and Rules
items.summary: Approved committee reports concerning targeted charter amendments for budgetary authority and mayoral appointment confirmations.

items.title: Public Hearing: Oasis Restaurant Special Permit
items.summary: The Council continued a public hearing for a special permit for extended hours at 373 Main Street to June 6 following extensive resident opposition regarding noise, parking, and a lack of code enforcement.

items.title: Secure Firearm Storage Resolution
items.summary: Passed a resolution requesting that the city implement a secure firearm storage program and distribute educational materials through public buildings and police licensing processes.

items.title: Medford High School Robotics Recognition
items.summary: Congratulated the Bowtech Robotics Team for winning the New England Regionals and qualifying for the World Championships.

items.title: Food Truck and Victualler's Licenses
items.summary: Approved a food truck permit for Cool Cow Ice Cream and a common victualler's license for LaBaguette Bakery at 428 Salem Street.

items.title: Zoning Map Change: 99 Revere Beach Parkway
items.summary: Referred a petition to rezone 4.5 acres at 99 Revere Beach Parkway to a mixed-use zone to the Community Development Board for further study.

items.title: Public Participation: Union Contract Negotiations
items.summary: Representatives from the clerical and DPW unions requested council support in settling contracts that have remained expired for four years, citing pay disparities and unfavorable working conditions.

items.title: Charter Amendment Public Hearings
items.summary: Opened and continued public hearings to June 6 regarding three proposed charter amendments concerning council staff, the budget process, and mayoral appointment confirmations.

items.title: Green Automotive Repair License
items.summary: Approved an auto repair license for 38 Linden Street with conditions restricting the site to mechanical repairs and stipulating the license remains with the current petitioner.

items.title: Routine Business and Tabled Items
items.summary: Tabled two zoning matters to June 6 and approved the acceptance of donated Pride Month stickers and pins.
